subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration readiness — Catalyst Bio sizing & cutover plan
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@catalystbio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <s.li@catalystbio.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted → Dedicated migration: initial sizing questions

Hi Marcus / Monica,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the team here at Catalyst liked the latency guarantees and the autoscale options. We are evaluating the move from your hosted API to a Dedicated pool for our production traffic (primary app: clinical annotations). Before we start formal procurement, procurement and engineering need a clear sizing validation plan and a cutover timeline we can sign off on.

High-level asks:
- A concise acceptance test matrix (what pass/fail looks like) we can run during the dry run
- Expected committed GPU SKUs and QPS/throughput targets per SKU
- Rollback window and estimated client-side impact for the swap
- What evidence you need from our side (sample traffic, prompts, eval set)

If you can outline a 2–3 week validation cadence and what artifacts we should expect to receive from Redwood, that would help lock dates internally. Looking to target an end-of-June migration but flexible if the validation requires more time.

Regards,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering | Catalyst Bio
[Attachment: catalyst-procurement-intent.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@catalystbio.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted → Dedicated migration: initial sizing questions

Tom — thanks, appreciated. Summary below of what Redwood will own for the validation + an initial 3-week cadence that maps to your asks. Please confirm the window you'd prefer and we will hold resources.

Proposed validation cadence (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 — Data/traffic handoff & model selection (you send sampled traffic + top 50 prompts)
   - Redwood: run profiling, propose GPU SKUs and quantization profile
2) Week 1 — Baseline capacity runs (staging dedicated pool)
   - Acceptance tests: 95th p99 latency target, sustained throughput at 70–80% of committed capacity, token-cost delta within agreed band
3) Week 2 — Cutover dry run & rollback rehearsal
   - Canary traffic (10–25%) for 4 hours, warm KV cache, failover to hosted in case of regressions

Key details / answers:
- SKUs: likely mix of a2-24 / g5-8 (finalized after profiling). We'll provide a short SKU-cost matrix.
- Rollback window: we recommend a 30–45 minute operational rollback with a pre-defined traffic-quiesce plan; we'll own the server-side rollback, you will toggle client routing for immediate rollback if desired.
- Evidence needed from you: 72-hour representative traffic dump (anonymized), top-50 prompt set, sample sessions for stateful workflows, and the eval questions set.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Sizing report (PDF) with SKU recommendation and stress-test results
- Cutover playbook (docx) with step-by-step runbook and rollback steps
- Traffic model CSV showing expected token distribution and QPS

Action item / owners (initial):
- Catalyst: provide traffic dump + prompt set by 2027-05-02 — Tom (owner)
- Redwood: profiling + preliminary SKU recommendation by 2027-05-06 — Marcus (owner)
- Redwood infra: schedule staging runs week of 2027-05-10 — Karthik (owner)
- Ops dry run / go/no-go meeting 2027-05-20 — Grace (owner)

We can shift the overall migration target to late June if you need more runway. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for the go/no-go.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sku-cost-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

Tom / Samantha — attaching the profiling report and the cutover playbook as promised. Key validation gates (from the playbook):

1) Throughput acceptance: sustained 4-hour run at 80% committed capacity with no >5% error-rate spikes
2) Latency guards: p95 under 220ms, p99 under 450ms for the annotated workload
3) Cache warmup: KV cache must reach 90% steady-state within the canary window (we provide warmup scripts)
4) Rollback rehearsal: successful rollback in under 30 minutes during staging without data loss (we will simulate client routing failure)

Attachments: [Attachment: catalyst-sizing-v1.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: redwood-cutover-playbook-v1.docx (docx)], [Attachment: traffic-model.csv (csv)]

Action items (owners & dates):
- Catalyst: deliver 72-hour anonymized traffic and sample session logs by 2027-05-02 — Tom (owner)
- Redwood profiling: final SKU selection & cost proposal by 2027-05-06 — Marcus (owner)
- Infra staging window booked for 2027-05-10 → 2027-05-12 — Karthik (owner)
- Ops dry run & rollback rehearsal: 2027-05-20 10:00AM PT — Grace (owner)

If everything passes the validation gates we recommend a target swap window during the following maintenance window: 2027-06-24 → 2027-06-26 (two-day window with final cut midday 2027-06-25). If you prefer a single-day cut, we can compress to 2027-06-25 but recommend extra canary time.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if you want to walk the playbook.

— Monica
